title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A/S is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over a base S of characteristic p>0. A is ordinary, i.e. generically ordinary in the sense of the previous page. The previous page states the canonical splitting D^1(A/S) = H^1_DR(A/S) ≅ t_A^∨ ⊕ t_{A*}, together with F_p-structures t_A ≅ L_A ⊗_{F_p} O_S and t_{A*} ≅ L_{A*} ⊗_{F_p} O_S. Here L_A and L_{A*} are étale-locally free F_p-sheaves of rank g. They come from the factorisation pA → (pA)_ét → S.

Step 1 (this page). There are canonical isomorphisms L_A = ((pA*)_ét)^∨ and L_{A*} = ((pA)_ét)^∨, where ^∨ is the F_p-linear dual of the étale F_p-sheaf.
- For L_{A*}: t_{A*} = H^1(A, O_A), and its Frobenius-fixed part is H^1_et(A, Z/p) = Hom(pA, Z/p) = Hom((pA)_ét, Z/p).
- For L_A: Lie(A) = Lie of the multiplicative part (pA)^0. By Cartier duality (pA)^0 is dual to (pA*)_ét. Since Lie(μ_p) = O_S has a canonical basis, Lie(pA^0) = ((pA*)_ét)^∨ ⊗ O_S.

Step 2 (N.B.). Let φ be a polarization, or more generally a section of NS_{A/S}. Its de Rham Chern class is a section φ' of Λ^2 H^1_DR = H^2_DR(A/S). The splitting gives Λ^2 DR^1 ≅ Λ^2 t_A^∨ ⊕ (t_A^∨ ⊗ t_{A*} = Hom(t_A, t_{A*})) ⊕ Λ^2 t_{A*}.
- Grothendieck says φ' lies in the middle term, i.e. in H^1(A, Ω^1) (Hodge type (1,1)).
- As one sees immediately, φ' is the tangent map Lie(φ̃): t_A → t_{A*} of φ̃ = λ_φ: A → A*.
- This tangent map is itself obtained by ⊗_{F_p} O_S from a map L_A → L_{A*}. That map is the F_p-dual of (pA)_ét → (pA*)_ét, which is induced by pφ̃: pA → pA*.

Purpose: the polarization respects the canonical (unit-root / étale-multiplicative) F_p-structure on Hodge cohomology of an ordinary abelian scheme. This is preparation for the next page. There Grothendieck builds, from the F_p-local system det((pA*)_ét), a canonical section of ω_A^{⊗(p-1)} on the ordinary locus, and extends it to all of S via Frobenius/Verschiebung on t_A, i.e. (det t_A)^{⊗p} → det t_A. That is the Hasse invariant.

A crossed-out first attempt used the alternating pairing to view H^{10} and H^{01} as isotropic subquotients. It got a map t_{A*} → t_A, the wrong direction/variance, and was abandoned.
errors: The middle summand is written 't_A ⊗ t_{A*}' with brace 'Hom(t_A, t_{A*})'. Correctly it is t_A^∨ ⊗ t_{A*} = Hom(t_A, t_{A*}), since Λ^2(t_A^∨ ⊕ t_{A*}) has middle term t_A^∨ ⊗ t_{A*}. This is a slip of a dual sign.
The crossed-out passage produced a map t_{A*} → t_A from the pairing t_A^∨ ⊗ t_{A*} → O_S, which has the wrong variance. Grothendieck discarded it himself.
No real gap otherwise. The claims are correct and standard for ordinary abelian schemes.

ideas.what: Canonical F_p-structures on Lie(A) and Lie(A*) for ordinary A, via the étale parts of p-torsion and Cartier duality: L_A = ((pA*)_ét)^∨ and L_{A*} = ((pA)_ét)^∨.
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root F-crystal / étale-multiplicative (connected-étale) decomposition of ordinary p-divisible groups; Serre–Tate theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate (1964), Messing, Katz ('Serre–Tate local moduli', 1981), Deligne–Illusie
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck's Montreal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1970/74) and ICM 1970 talk; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Splitting of H^1_DR of an ordinary abelian scheme into t_A^∨ ⊕ t_{A*}, and the induced splitting of Λ^2.
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root splitting of the Hodge filtration (Hodge vs conjugate filtration splitting in the ordinary case)

ideas.what: The de Rham Chern class of a polarization lies in H^1(Ω^1) = Hom(t_A, t_{A*}) and equals the tangent map of λ_φ: A → A*. In the ordinary case it descends to an F_p-map induced by pλ_φ on étale parts.
ideas.modern_name: Chern class of a polarization = Lie(λ_L); compatibility of polarization with unit-root structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Mumford, Oda 1969 'The first de Rham cohomology group...', Berthelot–Breen–Messing)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification inside Grothendieck's exploration of Barsotti–Tate groups. It covers the canonical F_p-structure on Hodge cohomology of ordinary abelian schemes and the compatibility of the polarization's Chern class with it. All of this is standard (Serre–Tate, Katz, Oda). The following page's Hasse invariant construction is also classical, and this page contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Ceci dit, φ' est dans le dernier ...' should read 'Ceci dit, φ' est dans le terme médian, et comme on le voit aussitôt n'est autre que l'homom. tangent φ̃' : t_A → t_{A*} de φ̃ : A → A* défini par φ'.
'par L_A → L_{A*} lui-même de' should read 'par L_A → L_{A*} lui-même [déduit/transposé] de (pA*)_ét^∨ → (pA)_ét^∨' (the transpose of (pA)_ét → (pA*)_ét induced by pφ̃).
The crossed-out word before ⊗_{F_p} O_S is 'par': 'par tensorisation [-par-] ⊗_{F_p} O_S'.
In the decomposition the middle term is written as t_A ⊗ t_{A*}, but mathematically it should be t_A^∨ ⊗ t_{A*} (Grothendieck's own slip or an unclear check mark).
First line: 'Ceci dit, on a des isom. can.' is correct. The isomorphisms are L_A = ((pA*)_ét)^∨ and L_{A*} = ((pA)_ét)^∨ (underlined script L).
